title: AI-assisted cerebellar atlases reveal primate-specific cellular organization
summary: Deep-learning segmentation and spatial annotation supported cerebellar atlases of macaques, marmosets and mice, revealing primate-specific cell subtypes and regional gene-expression differences. Transcriptomic gradients corresponded with awake functional-connectivity patterns. This represents the September 27, 2024 journal version; an institutional announcement gives September 26, and the observed associations do not establish causal functions.
organization: BGI-Research; Chinese Academy of Sciences; Erasmus MC; Tencent AI Lab

evidence.tested: New spatial tissue measurements, biological replicates and comparisons with awake fMRI supported the reported anatomical associations within this study.
evidence.unknown: Not assessed: exhaustive supplements, earlier-preprint chronology and independent confirmation. Functional mechanisms are not established by spatial correlations.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning models segment cells; STAGATE clusters spatial domains and DestVI assigns cell-type probabilities.
